decisions.statement: `undefined` takes its place.
`undefined` is the single spelling a body returning something cannot fill.
An async body is the case this rule is for.
Every failure inside the async body goes unheard.
Only a function whose body is written here is judged.
A declaration has a body written here.
A function expression has a body written here.
An arrow has a body written here.
A method has a body written here.
A getter has a body written here.
An overload signature is judged with the body the overload signature heads.
A function type describes a function written elsewhere.
A method signature describes a function written elsewhere.
A call signature describes a function written elsewhere.
A constructor type describes a function written elsewhere.
An ambient declaration describes a function written elsewhere.
Every declaration a declaration file carries is ambient.
A type describing a function written elsewhere is left.
A callback a caller fills is such a type.
A function answering `void` fits no slot spelled `undefined`.
The line named is the annotation's own rather than the function's.
`void` reached as a type argument is left.
`Promise<void>` is the case left most often.
`void` used as an operator on an expression is untouched.
`void` used as an operator on an expression is no type at all.
A body filling a slot spelled `void` and dropping a promise is left.

definition: the rule refusing `void` where a function written here states its return type
